sources.entry: Clipy - Clipy is a Clipboard extension app for macOS.

summary.one_liner: Clipy is a clipboard extension app for macOS that keeps clipboard history and saved snippets, opened through global keyboard shortcuts.
summary.what_it_does: Clipy runs as a macOS menu bar clipboard extension. It provides a main menu, a clipboard history menu, and a snippets menu, each opened with a default keyboard shortcut (Shift+Command+V, Control+Command+V, and Shift+Command+B respectively). A separate Settings shortcut (Control+Option+Shift+Command+V) opens Settings even when the menu bar icon is hidden. All shortcuts can be changed under Settings > Shortcuts, except the Settings shortcut, which can be changed but not removed. The README describes building the app from source in Xcode, with ad-hoc signing for local builds, and optional Firebase integration via a user-supplied GoogleService-Info.plist. It is MIT licensed and is a derivative of ClipMenu, which the README credits.
use_cases: keep a history of copied text on a Mac
paste a previously copied item again
open clipboard history with a keyboard shortcut
build a clipboard manager from source
how_to_run: Open Configurations/CodeSigning.xcconfig and uncomment #include "Configurations/CodeSigning-AdHoc.xcconfig" for ad-hoc builds.
Build the Clipy scheme in Xcode.
Optionally place your own GoogleService-Info.plist in Clipy/GoogleService if you want Firebase features.
notable: Default global shortcuts for main menu, clipboard history, snippets, and settings
Settings shortcut stays available even if the menu bar icon is hidden
Ad-hoc signing setup so Accessibility permission is not re-requested on every build
Derived from ClipMenu, with the README asking forks not to use the Clipy or ClipMenu names
caveats: Local builds need switching to ad-hoc signing because the Clipy signing certificate is available only to the maintainer
Optional Firebase features need your own GoogleService-Info.plist
